My top 13:      * **A book about sports history** by a political writer. This author went to a foreign country for a few years to complete this English language book about the history of the sport behind the Iron Curtain. Incredible book. If you liked the documentary this is a must-read, as it's way, way better than that mediocre documentary.   * **A book by a famous coach** by a former coach. Very hard to find and very expensive if you do. Translated in the 1960s and way out of print. The architect of the sports machine describes his sports program and gives his thoughts on various other countries' sports programs - apparently he admired the players from another country and thought Canadians were barbarians. Who knew?   * **A biography of a famous defenseman** by a biographer. Biography of the late defenseman and Hall of Famer who also founded a local donut/coffee chain. Goes into tremendous detail as the author always does, and gives a good rundown of the forms, which was the system used by teams to acquire players before the entry draft was a thing.   * **A biography of a famous captain** by a biographer. He uses the career of a famous captain as a vehicle to analyze the transformation of a local organization from perennial loser to unstoppable juggernaut. Even goes into details on the executive careers of various executives.   * **A history of a rival league** by a historian. Consummate history of the WHA. Perfectly made book, everything you'd ever want to know.   * **A book about the business of sports**, by two authors. Similar to the popular book Business Adventures by John Brooks, but sports-themed. A handful of excellent stories related to the business aspect of the league.   * **A book by a former commissioner** by a former league executive and one-time commissioner of the league. Some of this book is obviously biased, as the author had recently been ousted as the commissioner and booted from the Hall of Fame, but there's tons of great info in here.   * **A famous book by a goalie** by a former goalie. Nothing needs to be said about this one.   * **A biography of a famous coach** by a biographer. Not perfect, since this book was finished in the 1990s so it's missing the 2002 Wings and his time as an executive with another team, but it does a flawless job of presenting a balanced account of the greatest coach in sports history.   * **A textbook on sports history**, multiple authors. Basically a textbook on the history of the game from the first puck drop to the year 2000. Goes over every major news story that happened and has nice biographies of every star player from each decade.   * **A tell-all book by a forward** // **A tell-all book by a forward** - tie. Great no holds-barred tell-all books by former star players who were never really good at keeping their mouths shut.   * **A book by a journeyman player** by a journeyman player. He may have only been a plug, but the author is a genuinely great storyteller and this book is enjoyable from start to finish. He had an interesting if not strange career.
